title: Zelensky signs Ukraine's new mobilisation law
body:
On 16 April 2024 Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky signed a law on military service, mobilisation and military registration. The Verkhovna Rada had adopted it on 11 April after more than 4,000 amendments were filed before the final reading. The law was to take effect one month after its publication.

Under the law, men must update their personal data with military authorities, payments to volunteers increase, and new punishments apply to draft dodging. Al Jazeera noted that the final text lacked the much tougher sanctions for evasion that had been in the initial draft. A separate law, signed shortly before, lowered the minimum mobilisation age from 27 to 25.

Ukraine began mobilising right after Russia's full-scale invasion in February 2022. Later, the number of volunteers fell and thousands of draft-evasion cases were reported. It was unclear how many additional soldiers the new provisions could mobilise, and analysts and some serving personnel doubted that the law would fully resolve troop shortages. Army chief Oleksandr Syrskyi said at the time that Russian troops aimed to capture Chasiv Yar by 9 May.
